event: US S&P Global flash PMIs (Nov, manufacturing/services/composite)
why: Early read on US factory demand, a driver for copper and steel sentiment.
Consumer outlook feeds dollar and growth expectations that move metals.

event: US initial jobless claims (moved up for Thanksgiving)
why: Labor-market signal shifts Fed-cut odds and the dollar.
Direct gauge of capital-goods and metal-intensive demand.

event: GDP Q3 second estimate + Personal Income & Outlays / PCE inflation (Oct)
why: Growth and the Fed's preferred inflation gauge drive rate expectations and the dollar.
Housing activity drives copper wiring/plumbing and steel demand.

event: Preliminary US imports of steel products (Oct)
why: Import volumes affect domestic HRC supply and pricing.
Anecdotal read on manufacturing/steel/construction ahead of the December FOMC.
source: Federal Reserve Beige Book page (Nov 25 date)

event: Thanksgiving: CME will not derive or disseminate settlements for CME, CBOT, NYMEX or COMEX; US stock and bond markets closed
why: Thin or no US trading means no official COMEX copper/HRC settles that day.

event: Advance economic indicators (Oct goods trade, retail and wholesale inventories)
why: Trade and inventory data feed Q4 GDP tracking and metal import demand.

event: Day after Thanksgiving: COMEX metals on normal settlement schedule; CME equity and interest-rate settlements at 12:00 CT; US stocks close early
why: Low liquidity can exaggerate metal price moves.

event: China NBS official manufacturing and non-manufacturing PMIs (Nov; listed as estimated)
why: China is the largest copper and steel consumer, so its factory data moves base metals.

event: China Caixin manufacturing PMI (Nov; listed as confirmed)
why: Private-sector China factory read, key for copper demand.
Headline US factory gauge, including prices paid for metals.
Construction is a top end-use for steel and copper.
Labor demand informs Fed path and dollar.
Private payroll preview ahead of the jobs report.
Broad economic momentum signal affecting rate and dollar expectations.
Final read on durable and nondurable orders tied to metal demand.
Biggest monthly macro data release, so it can swing the dollar and metals sharply ahead of the December FOMC.
